Unconventional: No

Comments: On April 13 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the CFR USX 5 OG Well in regards to violations issued under inspection report 4157445. Accompanying me in today's inspection is Rosie Wise (PaDEP)The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department again observed the water flowing onto the access road. It did not appear any remedial actions have been taken to address the flowing water and resulting erosion and sedimentation issues on the access road.As previously described in IR 4157445:The water was observed flowing down the access road where it appeared to end at the well site. Erosion channels appear to have formed along the access road as a result of the flowing water. The water appears to be originating from a drainage channel/tributary to Antram Run. It appears that a culvert located under the access road may be damaged or obstructed, causing the water to flow onto the access road rather than through the culvert. The Department was unable to locate/inspect the culvert inlet. However, no water was observed discharging from the culvert outlet.Upon inspection of the well posting, it appeared a new well posting has been installed on a piece of the production equipment in accordance with OGA3211(H). The well posting appeared to contain the well permit number, operator's name, and operator's phone number. However, it did not appear to contain the operator's address. The Department recommends the operator ensure all required information is properly posted in accordance with OGA3211(G).Based on today's inspection, OGA3211(H) is being closed. All other violations issued in IR 4157445 remain outstanding.

Comments: Onsite for a routine inspection. A 140bbl steel tank, 50bbl poly tank, and a separator are surrounded by an earthen dike. The steel tank has several small rusted out holes on the backside of the tank. A rusty blister (hole developing from corrosion) was observed to be leaking fluid down the side of the tank. The violation has been corrected.

Comments: The site of this oil spill is in a forested area on an access road south off Center Hill Road, 430 yards on south branch of access. Will Warfel contacted WQS Taylor and reported to National Response Center that there was a release of about 20 gallons of crude oil from a tank the wind tipped over in one of the recent storms. The path of the crude oil was ~320 yards on the access from origin of the spill to low spot where it left the road and seeped into the stream. Blobs of oily material were found ~60 yards downstream. Two absorbent booms were placed in the stream along with absorbent pads. One absorbent boom was placed across the access road and one was positioned along the road to catch any remaining oil from seeping to stream. Visual clean-up of oil and oil contaminated soil completed where the tank tipped and leaked oil. The tank was removed and contaminated soil piled and covered until soil is tested and can be received at a licensed facility.Violations for the release of oil to ground and into a stream issued with this inspection. Clean-up, restoration and stabilization of spill site with vegetation and receipt of tipping receipts and waste manifest by the Department required to lift violations.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/30/2024 to ARMAC RESOURCES LLC in Warren City, Warren county. 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARMAC RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/30/2024
Violation Code: 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 8189615
Permit API: 123-45286
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Warren City
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/30/2024
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an active stray gas migration case (CTS# 369563). Previously this well was found to have methane detected outside of the well bore and the operator decided to plug the well. Upon completion of their plugging attempt they inadvertently cemented some of their tubing into the well. Subsequently a camera was ran into the well and bubbles were visibly seen at the top of fluid level. A MSA Altair 5X gas meter was used and determined the bubbles were methane being emitted into the well bore. A violation was issued to the operator for not properly plugging the well. To address this violation the operator had a rig attempt to drill down to approx 550', which is 50' below the surface casing shoe and remove the cemented in tubing at which point another camera run would have taken place to see if the well is still bubbling methane. The rig failed to drill down to 550' and it was decided to cement the remaining tubing into the well. Top of cement was then at 288.23' with approx. 102' of tubing encapsulated within the well bore. ARMAC then contracted Hornburg Drilling to drill and clean out the well-bore to a depth of 560'. This was completed, however a stray gas zone was detected at approximately 550' from a previous gamma ray log and it was decided to add 10 sacks of Type 1 cement to cover this stray gas zone. At the time of inspection J and D Services was rigged up onto the well with their rig and tagged the top of cement at 560'. They then pulled their cement tubing to 559' and pumped a 10 sack slurry and pulled to 510' and rolled the hole and washed off with 25 bbls of freshwater. J and D Services will tag top of cement at a later date and report back to the Department.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8155846
Permit API: 015-23794
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/16/2023
Comments: On 8/16/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Deremer well site. It was 73 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. Heavy rainfall has been reported in the region within the last 48 hours and there were water puddles scattered across the pad surface.The Chesapeake company man, Fletcher Brand, explained current operations as follows: A Haliburton frac fleet was on site fracking four newly drilled wells. Three existing wells are shut in but were still staged for production. The frac crew was zippering between the four wells, fracking a stage and jumping to another well. Wireline was staying ahead, prepping the wells ahead of the frac operations. They have completed 37 stages of 327 total stages. Fletcher expects to be onsite another 27 days.Due to fracking requirements at the time of the inspection, Fletcher could not accompany me during the inspection. I started the inspection unaccompanied and was met by the Chesapeake HSE, Chris Bass, as I was viewing the site.I viewed the brine unloading area. Trucks were backed into the station and were being offloaded during the inspection. I field tested water/mud puddles in this area for conductivity with results being at 0.5 mS. Frac and wireline operations were being conducted on plastic lined secondary containment that was protected by drilling mats. The brine tanks were stationed in plastic lined secondary containment. During the inspection, I did witness a 75' x 30' x 1" deep interconnected stream of water puddles on the unprotected pad surface that ran along the south edge of the brine tank secondary containment and continued southeast for approximately 30'. The puddle field tested at 3.13 mS conductance in the approximate center near the southeast corner of the brine tanks. I collected sample 9551-056 from the water puddle for laboratory analysis.I viewed the chemical additive area. Water on the unprotected ground in this area field tested at 0.6 mS conductance or less.Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover with steeper sections of the fill slope stabilized with rock. PCSM is addressed on site by four retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface is a violation of CSL 402(b). Because of the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface.Violations cited in inspection report 3558977 on 5/23/2023 are still outstanding for the site for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface during drilling operations.I left the site at 1420 hours.

Inspection Date: 2020-02-24
Comments: On February 24, 2020 , DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an inspection for a reported spill (CTS at 348187) at Beech Resources Premier Well Pad. At the time of inspection, the operator was in the process of rigging down the site from the recent stimulation of the wells onsite. The DEP met with Don Stevenson of Beech Resources. He explained that some hoses were disconnected from the blender and were not drained of production fluid. The hoses were not completely placed on containment and spilled about 30 gallons of brine water outside of containment. The operator was in the process of vacuuming the containment. Once that has been completed the containment will be removed and the excavation of the impacted area will begin. Penn E&R is scheduled to collect biased samples of the impacted area. DEP conducted field screening of the puddles in the area where the hoses spilled the brine water for conductivity. The puddles tested returned an over range reading of the conductivity meter (>19.99 mS/cm). Beech Resources plans to excavate the impacted soil to below a soil conductivity of 1000 uS/cm. February 25, 2020 The DEP received an email from Don Stevenson with pictures showing the excavation of the impacted area from the spill the evening of 2/24/2020. The DEP followed up with a site visit to confirm the excavation. At the time of the visit, Penn E&R was onsite continuing the conductivity delineation of the spill. The operator was also continuing to excavate impacted soil from the spill. The area that has been excavated is about a 20' x 30' area at a depth of less than a foot. Penn E&R stated that five 10 yard roll off dumpsters have been filled with impacted soil to this point. More excavation is going to be required to remove the remaining impacted soil. The DEP screened the area of the spill, which resulted in a range of 200 uS/cm to areas that were over range of the meter(>4.00 mS/cm). Before leaving the well pad, the DEP spoke with Don Stevenson on the phone and explained with the area excavated and the amount of impacted soil collected that the DEP recommends starting the Act 2 process. The spill of production fluid from the hoses outside of containment is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), §78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301.

Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 879709
Permit API: 125-27614
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Chartiers Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-03-05
Comments: On March 4, 2020, the Operator reported the following: “The incident occurred at the Moritz Well Pad. Reportedly, 126 gallons of produced water was released while GPUs were being blown down. A 1/2 valve was left open and the produced water back fed into the GPU line and was released to the GPU skid and gravel pad. All produced water was reportedly removed. Range is prepared to rig down GPU's for remediation. A vac truck is on standby in case heavy precipitation event occurs overnight. Crews will be on scene tomorrow. No waterways reportedly impacted.” On March 5, 2020, I conducted a follow up inspection to a release of fluid to the well pad reported on 3/4/2020. I was accompanied by Range representative Brandon Carson. According to Mr. Carson a needle valve on the 3H GPU was left open after it was blown down for snubbing operation, snubbing is act of adding a smaller diameter tubing to a well to increase the flow rate of the well. The release occurred when the common dump line flowed back into the 3H GPU, overflowing the 3H GPU and causing fluid to be lost to the well pad surface via an open needle valve on the 3H GPU. The GPUs were not placed in secondary containment at the time of the release. During the inspection, the Operator was working to disconnect the 3H GPU to move the unit and remediate the impacted location. No waterways were impacted by the release. The Operator is incompliance with the current spill policy and intends to utilize Act 2 for remediation of a release greater than 42 gallons. Violations are being issued for the release of a regulated fluid to the ground. - Invalid Complaint Id. - 348342

Comments: On 07/18/2023, an incident inspection was conducted at the Ironman Well Site in response to an incident report received by the Department and submitted by EQT on 07/17/2023 (CTS: 373620). I was accompanied by Matt Dracup, PGM (PADEP), Doug Oberdorf, and Jason Nicholson (EQT). Additional EQT and SPSI representatives on site. Stressed vegetation observed on north-northwest facing slope (fill side) of the Ironman pad on 07/14/2023 by an EQT contractor doing a routine site inspection. EQT representative investigated stressed vegetation on 07/17/2023 and identified it as a brine release and notified the Department. It was further investigated by EQT on 07/17/2023 w/ interim remediation activities starting on 07/18/2023. According to EQT, an approx. 5 ft x 2 ft pool of fluid was observed within area of stressed vegetation and fluid was observed sprinkling out. The overall area of stressed vegetation was approximately 25 ft x 25 ft. The release was estimated over a barrel and Act 2 remediation is anticipated. The source of the leak was identified as a small pinhole in cushion elbow at the northern most corner of the pad from the buried common dump line transferring brine flowback from the GPUs to the ASTs; approx. 70 ft northeast, away from the stressed vegetation area. Operator discovery and pre-remediation conductivity levels and incident writeup requested.Inspection observations: Area of stressed vegetation and pooled production fluid observed on fill slope below northwestern edge of pad and below compressor building on the pad. Among pooled fluid, an oily sheen was also observed. The impacted area appeared to be approx. 25 ft. x 25 ft. The area was covered with a plastic tarp upon arriving on site (Photos 1-7). SPSI crew preparing and beginning excavation to locate source of leak and begin remediation measures. Potholes to be dug on pad around approximate area of leak source to gain extent of fluid. Elevated conductivity observed within impacted area yielded readings of 14.62 mS, 9.96 mS. Readings beyond edge of impacted area, on the more northern edge of the area, displayed a reading of 1.87 mS. Violation ID: 875281

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 2020-01-27
Comments: On 1/27/19 at 0945 hrs., I conducted an inspection in response to a crude oil release that was reported to the Department on 1/25/20, and initially was discovered on 1/24/20. The release occurred near Howard Drilling, Inc.'s TLC 1 well (API 063-32818) in Conemaugh Twp., Indiana Co. According to initial reports, and verified by Mr. Dale "Wally" Howard via telephone on 1/27/20, approximately 80 barrels of crude oil was transferred from stock tanks at two nearby wells (063-22666 and 063-31878) during plugging operations, to two 100 barrel holding tanks located adjacent to Hogue Drive. According to Mr. Howard, the holding tanks belong to Tunnelton Liquids Company (property owner). ARG Refining was scheduled to pick the oil up on 1/24/20. The driver notified Howard Drilling on 1/24/20 that the tanks were empty. The driver then walked over to the release area and confirmed that crude oil had been released from the tanks, but was uncertain of he extent of the release. Mr. Howard had crews onsite on 1/24/20 and notified the Department of the release on 1/25/20. According to Mr. Howard, the driver reported that the valve to the tanks was open and a hose was connected to the tank valve and led to a drain in the adjacent cement pad. The crude oil flowed through the drain, under Hogue Drive and around a concrete secondary containment structure. The oil then flowed South through an old mine drainage treatment pond, and into a canal, which drains to the Conemaugh. McCutcheon Enterprises was contracted by Howard Drilling on 1/25/20 to begin the cleanup process. During my inspection, McCutcheon was in the process of excavating surface soils. In addition to the excavation, McCutcheon was also going to replace the underflow dam with one made of sand-filled super sacs. There was concern that the original dam was constructed with contaminated soil and this material was to be removed. McCutcheon was also conducting boom maintenance along the spill path. During my inspection, it was evident that some residual crude material remained in the drainage canal south of the release site; however, had still not made it to the down-gradient culvert leading to the Conemaugh River. The release of crude oil onto the ground and into waters of the Commonwealth constitutes violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), and SWMA 610(1). Mr. Howard had crews onsite on 1/24/20 and notified the Department of the release on 1/25/20. Comments: On January 13 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Aphrodite Well Site (ESCGP issued on 5/9/2020, amended on 2/5/2024, expiring on 2/4/2029) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 1/12/2026 (CTS 394575). Present during the inspection was operator representative Justin Miller.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel.At the time of inspection, there are 5 total wells on the well pad. According to the operator, stimulation for all 5 wells has been completed and they are preparing to conduct drill outs and flowback operations over the next 3 weeks.Upon inspection, it appeared the stimulation equipment was being demobilized. The drilling equipment still onsite appeared to be within secondary containment. The secondary containment appeared to be installed correctly with no tears or leaks. During the inspection, Mr. Miller guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Miller the release occurred on 1/13/2026. He stated the release occurred from a loose hose connection from one of the tanks. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 15 gallons of a produced water was released to the graveled well pad.The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the spill was in an approximate 4 foot by 20 foot area outside of the secondary containment for the tanks next to a GPU. Conductivity readings including several readings of OR (Over Detectable Range, >20MS) , 11.46mS, and 1.57mS, were obtained in the area of the release. During the inspection, the Department observed 2 small areas of excavation. Mr. Miller stated that additional excavation will occur as needed when the containment is removed from its location.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued against the Aphodite 2M well for the observed release.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/16/2023 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Wyalusing Township, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/16/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8155745
Permit API: 015-23849
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wyalusing Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/16/2023
Comments: On 8/16/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Roeber well site. It was 68 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. Heavy rainfall had impacted the region within the last 48 hours and water puddles were scattered around the pad surface.Chesapeake's company man, Buck Davis.explained operations as follows: The Patterson 583 drilling rig is drilling the first of two wells and was approximately 100 feet trom total depth. The one existing well, the Roeber 5H, has been shut in during the drilling process.Before I started the site inspection, a group of local dignitaries including a congressman and a Bradford County commissioner arrived at the site. I was allowed to conduct the site inspection unaccompanied while Chesapeake personnel guided the group through the site.I field tested water puddles near the cement silos and the cement unloading area with results at 0.4 mS conductance or less. Chemicals are stored and added to the process, all operations conducted over secondary containment. I did witness a water puddle on the north edge of the site that field tested at 1.738 mS conductance. There was a rainbow colored sheen and a brown shiny surface layer on some areas of this water puddle. It extended about 30 feet from the chemical storage secondary containment to the edge of the perimeter berm. I did not see the water puddle flowing off pad. The water puddle was as much as 2 inches deep and as much is 5 feet wide in spots. There was a visible flow of water coming from the chemical storage secondary containment leading into this water puddle. The Secondary containment structure did not have the plastic supported in this area to prevent fluid from escaping the containment. I collected sample number 9551055 from the puddled area that was closest to the secondary containment. The conductivity reading in this area was 1.671 mS. There was more visible evidence of a rainbow colored sheen and brown shiny surface layer in this area. As I was finishing collecting the sample, I was met by Eric Hottenstein and Eric Haskins. After explaining what I had found, they did say that the free liquids would be sucked up and the area scraped. They also said that the chemical secondary containment would be repaired. Before I left the site, the plastic liner was supported to allow for the secondary containment structure to contain fluids again. Buck was arranging for a vac truck to remove the free liquids. There were eight frac tanks on site being used for return water. These were located in secondary containment. Drill cuttings were being collected in rolloff dumpsters. They were being solidified and temporarily stored before being loaded for disposal; all of this conducted over secondary containment. The level of drill cuttings piled up in one of the dumpsters was above the height of the sides of the dumpster. I did discuss with Buck about having this level within the confines of the dumpster and allowing for some free board. A 3' x 5' water puddle near the entryway into the drill cutting area feel tested at 1.0 mS conductance. Other water puddles on the south side of the site field tested at 0.5 mS conductance or less.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover with the steep sections of the cut slope and fill slope stabilized with rock. PCSM is addressed by two retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the unprotected pad surface is a violation of CSL 402[b)Because of the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface. I left the site at 1230 hours.

Violation ID: 8249433
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/18/2025
Comments: The purpose of this routine inspection is to document a surface water encroachment resulting from the construction of the Akins Lease Akins #3 OG Well well pad. The well permit for Akins #3 was not observed anywhere onsite at the time of this inspection. Surface permitting biologists Samantha Lutz (DEP) and Jessica McDuff (DEP) were onsite for the duration of the inspection to confirm findings documented in the 08/04/2025 pre-construction inspection (Inspection # 4028638). Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) was also present. Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) arrived midway through the inspection.TMP opted to ignore advice given through the 08/04/2025 pre-construction inspection report and an 08/26/2025 field meeting. During the 08/26/2025 field meeting I advised Kyle Miller of the existing surface concerns in the vicinity of the staked well location, and made recommendations for maintaining appropriate setback distances per chapter 105 regulations.At the time of this inspection, it was observed that the well pad was constructed atop an unnamed tributary of Jackson Run pictured in the 08/04/2025 inspection images. The defined bed and banks of this stream are visible above the cut bank of the constructed well pad (Image 4), which suggests that excavation of the stream bed occurred during the construction of this well pad. It was also observed that dirt and gravel fill material was used to build up the site of the well pad atop the stream.A diversion ditch was constructed along the upslope perimeter of the well pad for the conveyance of roadway and well pad runoff, and apparently to accept the flow of the tributary stream that terminates abruptly on the cut bank of the well pad. This diversion ditch is then directed into a culvert on the west edge of the well site (Image 2). Comments: Inspection of Chesapeake's "Jads" Marcellus well site.Aaron Stredny (Chesapeake) called the DEP on Friday August 19, 2022 to report an estimated 50 gallon spill of diesel fuel. The spill happened when a fuel tank fell off a forklift. A vac truck already on site removed the standing liquid fuel, they also used absorbent pads on the fuel.I spoke with Danny Lambert (Company Man) on site. He showed me where the fuel spill occurred, which is now a water puddle. I did not see any sheen or evidence of residual fuel on the pad. A MiniRae 3000 photoionization detector with a 10.6 eV bulb returned 0.0 ppm readings from the spill area, indicating absence of volatiles emitting from that area. Creston Environmental is arriving tomorrow to delineate the impacted pad area for excavation and sampling. Nabors' X25 rig is installing production casing in the the 3rd of 6 Marcellus wells here today. Tomorrow they start drilling the 4th well. They drill on water/bentonite until ~7,000' depth, then switch to diesel based mud for "kickoff" into the horizontal section. Lambert expects to finish drilling here in October 2022.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.I did not see any Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls in place.Pooled on the pad surface in 5 separate areas has electrical conductivity of 0.46-0.67 mS/cm with an Oakton PCSTestr 35. Air temp 79FJLP

Comments: On May 12, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 4178724.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. CFS is not observed in these two areas.- The third area of accelerated erosion appears to be experiencing vegetative growth after it was observed to be seeded and mulched during the previous inspection (Photos 7-8). CFS appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time.- Additional CFS that was installed along the access road near the gated entrance (Photo 9) and appears to still be installed and functioning properly at this time.- E and S Plan is present on-site.- The well site and access road from the gate to the site appears to have been seeded and mulched. Vegetative growth appears to be progressing on this section of the access road and on site. - Production tank appears to have been removed on site and the earthen berm area has been regraded. No spills, leaks, or releases are observed at this time.- Well appears to be buried at this time (Photo 18).- CFS on-site appears to be installed and functioning properly. No E and S issues observed on site at this time.The Department recommends the operator stabilize the two points of accelerated erosion and sedimentation and install CFS per the E and S Plan. Violations remain outstanding for accelerated erosion and sedimentation along the access road and for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S Plan.

Comments: On November 26, 2024, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a referral from OGI Charles Reaggle (IR 3864611 on 10/18/2024). OGI Charles Reaggle requested that a WQS follow up because of observed fluid dripping from both annulus wings. Well appears to be equipped for production. Site is well vegetated.Well tag requirement fulfilled with API number present on production tank. Well posting for Big Dog Energy does not appear to be correct Operator. In IR 3864611, the Department noted that the well transferred Operators from Big Dog Energy to Dorso LP, however the well has since transferred again to Apollo Resources as of October 30, 2024. The Department recommends Apollo Resources fulfill the well posting requirement in accordance with OGA3211(G).Drip still observed coming from the annulus. Specific conductivity was measured inside the annulus (7.62 mS / 7,620 uS), in the soil below the annulus (1.161 mS / 1,161 uS), and three background points of the soil surrounding the site (0.1805 mS / 180.5 uS), (0.1524 mS / 152.4 uS), (0.262 mS / 262 uS). These measurements of specific conductivity indicate that a release of brine has occurred from the annulus. The Department recommends the Operator repair the annulus to prevent further release. The Department recommends the Operator remove all impacted soil/material and properly disposing of the soil/material.Production tank on site and appears to be structurally sound at this time. Violations are being issued for release of production fluid to the ground. Previously issued violations in IR 3864611 by OGI Charles Reaggle are being evaluated under enforcement ID 435756.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On 4/26/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an Administrative inspection on the Chesapeake Grippo well site. This inspection is to report the results of one water sample that was collected from a 60' x 60' water/ice puddle that was located southeast of the well heads and adjacent to the south edge of secondary containment for six frac tanks.During an inspection on 3/30/2023, the department discovered elevated conductance fluid on the well pad surface outside of containment. The fluid covered a 60' x 60' area and field tested at 4.05 mS conductance with an Oakton PCTS-50 meter. The department collected water sample #9551-049 for laboratory analysis from location Lat: 41.64109 Long: -76.35054. On 4/20/2023 the department received the results of the laboratory analysis that shows elevated barium, strontium, lithium and chlorides and is indicative of brine/production fluid being released onto the pad. The sample report is displayed in pictures 5 and 6. Chesapeake is pursuing Act 2 for the site in response to that incident.The release of fluid with elevated conductance to the pad surface during production operations constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.57(a) and 78a.66(b)(2).Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3529982 for elevated conductance fluid being discovered on the unprotected pad surface and for inspection ID 3517519 for high conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface after fracking operations and for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface during drilling operations.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going gas migration case. At the time of inspection I observed a cable rig rigged up over the well and the well shut in. A slam bar hole was placed 1.5' from the well and was metered with and ALTAIR 5X five sensor meter. At this slam bar hole 100% methane was detected. I then put a series of slam bar holes (12 total) radiating outward from the well. At points 50' from the well no gas was detected. I spoke with Justin Hanson of Bull Run Energy who does all the well tending in this area for Armac and he stated that they were going to run a cement bond log on this well tomorrow (03/14/2023).
